questions.q: What problem does Docker Compose solve, according to this lesson?
options: It makes a single container start faster
It replaces a wall of individual `docker run` commands with one file describing every service together
It removes the need to write a Dockerfile
It automatically scales containers across multiple servers
questions.explain: Compose describes every container (service) in a multi-container app in one file, started together with one command.

questions.q: In the example compose.yaml, what's the difference between the `api` and `redis` services?
options: api pulls a published image; redis builds from a Dockerfile
There is no difference — both behave identically
api builds from a local Dockerfile; redis pulls a published image
redis requires a separate docker run command; api does not
questions.explain: `build: .` builds from the local Dockerfile, while `image: redis:7-alpine` pulls an already-published image — the two ways a service can get its container.

questions.q: What does `depends_on` control in a compose.yaml file?
options: Which service gets more CPU and memory
The start order between services
Which service's logs are shown by default
Whether a service is rebuilt on every `up`
questions.explain: depends_on tells Compose to start one service before another — in the example, redis starts before api.

questions.q: Which command stops and removes every container a compose.yaml file describes?
options: docker compose ps
docker compose logs
docker compose up -d
docker compose down
questions.explain: docker compose down is the cleanup command — it removes every container the file describes, by name, in one step.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how does Docker Desktop's Containers view treat a container started by `docker compose up` versus one started by `docker run`?
options: Identically — both show up in the exact same Containers view
Compose-started containers are hidden from the Containers view entirely
Compose-started containers appear in a completely separate, Compose-only view
Only `docker run` containers can be inspected with `docker exec`
questions.explain: Compose is a convenience layer, not a different kind of container — every service it starts lands in the same Containers view and works with the same docker logs/exec/stop commands.
